## MPC design system (@mpc/design 0.3.0)

This project follows the MPC design system. The rules below are mandatory.

### Colour and dimensions

- Author every colour as a token. No literal colour values.
- Available CSS variables: `--background`, `--foreground`, `--surface`, `--surface-elevated`, `--card`, `--card-foreground`, `--popover`, `--popover-foreground`, `--primary`, `--primary-foreground`, `--secondary`, `--secondary-foreground`, `--muted`, `--muted-foreground`, `--accent`, `--accent-foreground`, `--copper`, `--copper-glow`, `--mark`, `--gold`, `--steppe`, `--sand`, `--positive`, `--alert`, `--destructive`, `--destructive-text`, `--destructive-foreground`, `--border`, `--border-strong`, `--input`, `--ring`
- Radius: `--radius-sm`, `--radius-md`, `--radius-lg`, `--radius-xl`, `--radius`. Never use a larger value on a rectangle; a shape that is a circle by meaning (status dot, avatar, radio, switch, diagram ring) stays a circle with `rounded-full`.
- Typefaces: `--font-sans`, `--font-display`, `--font-mono`.
- Full list and the use of each token: see `docs/tokens.md`.

### Construction

- Author colour as a token, never as a literal — with one exception below.
- The exception: the whitepaper viewer (`.wp-*`) fixes its colours on purpose.
- Every animated utility must have a `prefers-reduced-motion` opt-out, and SSR must render the final state.
- Section rhythm is fixed: `py-24 lg:py-32`, separated by a hairline.
- Rhythm exceptions — the only places a section may leave `py-24 lg:py-32`: the home hero ends at `lg:pb-12`; logo strips (partners, backers) run `py-10 lg:py-12`; a page head runs `pt-16 pb-14 lg:pt-20 lg:pb-16` with no hairline; the first section after a page head opens at `pt-12`; rows inside a list carry row padding.
- Content width is `max-w-7xl px-6 lg:px-10`. Nothing sets its own container; a documentation shell divides this one into rails and a column, under the width budget below.
- A documentation shell with side rails keeps the content edge and a reading column of at least 40rem, even with a classic scrollbar. Inside `max-w-7xl px-6 lg:px-10` that is a width budget with 1rem left for the scrollbar, counting the column's padding on both sides (`lg:px-8` = 4rem): at `lg` (59rem inside the container padding) the left rail plus that padding take at most 18rem; from `xl` up (75rem, the container's cap) both rails plus that padding take at most 34rem. A shell that fits: left rail `14rem` from `lg`, right "on this page" rail `15rem` from `xl`, column `lg:px-8` — 41rem of text at `lg` and 42rem from `xl` up, about 40rem and 41rem behind a 15px scrollbar.
- The radius scale is for rectangles. A shape that is a circle by meaning — a status dot, an avatar, a radio button, a switch, a ring in a diagram — stays a circle, drawn with `rounded-full`; a rectangle never rounds past `--radius-xl`.
- Status colour is fixed by meaning: complete or confirmed → `--positive`; in progress or provisional → `--alert`; planned or designed → `--muted-foreground`; failed → `--destructive-text`. Copper, gold and steppe never carry a status. Every status also states its word — Completed, In progress, Planned — so colour is never the only channel; each of the four colours clears 4.5:1 on the background, so the word stays readable. The motion utilities follow the same map: `.node-pulse` marks the in-progress stage and takes `--alert`; `.live-dot` (`--positive`) means a system running now, such as a live feed, and is not a completion mark.

### Component layers

- **Shells** — Own the LocaleProvider, the Nav/Footer frame, and section order. A route file should render a shell and nothing else.
- **Chrome** — Rendered by every shell. Links come from one navigation registry, never from a local list.
- **Sections** — One argument each, opened by a `.label-eyebrow`. Carry `py-24 lg:py-32` and a hairline, except where the rhythm exceptions rule says otherwise; do not set a custom container.
- **Figures** — SVG and CSS only — no charting dependency. Must collapse to a readable static diagram under reduced motion.
- **Decorative art** — Carries no information, so it may draw on canvas or WebGL. `aria-hidden`; the copy beside it reads on its own; colours come from tokens at runtime; it pauses off screen, draws one still frame under reduced motion, and draws nothing without WebGL while the layout holds.
- **Overlays** — Exactly one may be visible at a time, and each declares how it yields to the others.
- **Behaviours** — Wrap content, never replace it. SSR emits the final state so nothing depends on client JS to become visible.

### Writing copy

Positioning: MPC is the mining RWA issuance standard infrastructure operating on blockchain.

Claims we do not make:

- Not a technology platform. Instead: Four operated layers — resource, structuring, tokenization, capital markets — as one standard stack.
- Not a single mine deal. Instead: Infrastructure that standardises verification across the mining-asset lifecycle. Any single project is a case, not the business.
- Not in issuance. Design & build stage. Instead: Readiness is disclosed item by item, including what is only provisionally selected. Never write in the present tense about a stage not reached.
- Not an offering or a solicitation. Instead: Institutional review briefs, due-diligence packages, and meetings. The disclaimer travels with every request surface.

Tone:

- State the stage in the same breath as the ambition.
- Every figure is verifiable or it does not appear.
- Name risks next to the structure that addresses them.
- Write for allocators: infrastructure vocabulary, not crypto vocabulary.
- No superlatives and no urgency devices.
- Fixed vocabulary: layer names, status words, and asset names are reused verbatim.
- Disclaimers are copy, not fine print. They sit in the paragraph.

Language:

- Copy lives in a `const COPY = { en: {...} } as const` beside its component, read with `useT`.
- State each fact in one wording — never let two surfaces phrase the same fact differently.
- Pages render `locale="en"`. English is the product language.
- Navigation labels come from a single registry, never from a local list.

### Logo

- Clearspace: 0.5× the mark's height on all sides, except in icon tiles, fixed headers and the compact lockup, which have their own rows below
- Minimum size — mark: 24px digital · 10mm print
- Minimum size — horizontal lockup: 120px wide digital · 32mm print
- Stacked lockup: Use above 96px wide only
- Lockup gap: 0.30× the mark's height between the mark and the wordmark
- Lockup wordmark: Wordmark height 0.44× the mark's height, centred on the mark's vertical centre
- Clearspace — icon tiles: Inside an icon tile (favicon, touch and app icons): 0.5× the mark's height from a 48px tile up; at least 0.15× from 32px to 47px; below 32px the mark keeps 24px and takes whatever space is left. Below 24px nothing meets the minimum until the small variant exists (#2)
- Clearspace — fixed headers: When a header bar shows the horizontal lockup file and is shorter than the lockup plus its clearspace: at least 0.125× the mark's height above and below; 0.5× to the side. Most headers use the compact lockup instead (next row)
- Compact lockup — headers and footers: In a header bar or a footer, the mark may stand beside "MPC" set as text instead of the horizontal lockup file: the mark file rendered 24–28px tall, "MPC" in the display face at weight 600 and 16px (or the wordmark file at the same height), 8–14px apart, both centred on one line. 0.5× the mark's height of clearspace to the side. The 120px lockup minimum and the lockup gap and wordmark ratios above do not apply to it

Don'ts:

- Rotate, skew, or otherwise distort the mark.
- Change stroke weights or redraw the interior facets.
- Add shadows, glows, outlines, or bevels.
- Recolour the mark outside the copper scale.
- Place the full-colour mark on photography — use a mono variant.
- Rearrange, resize, or re-space the mark against the wordmark — except as the compact lockup in headers and footers.
- Set the wordmark in a substitute typeface.
